candidates.name: Thames Barrier
candidates.story: Engineers used gates that rotate up from the riverbed to block storm surges while leaving navigation spans clear when open. The barrier became operational in 1982 and officially opened in 1984.
candidates.art_direction: Show a raised steel gate between two of the silver piers from a low river viewpoint so the gate profile is visible.

candidates.name: Abu Simbel Temples Relocation
candidates.story: Crews cut the two rock temples into more than a thousand blocks and reassembled them inside an artificial hill on higher ground, above the rising reservoir. The relocated temples were inaugurated on 22 September 1968.
candidates.art_direction: Use the contractor archive to show the Great Temple's partly rebuilt sandstone facade with lifting gear and visible block joints. Set the new site high above the reservoir, with the protective concrete dome still exposed behind the facade where the construction stage supports it.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre · Working Together: Abu Simbel
CNRS–INHA InVisu · Contractor archive of the Great Temple reconstruction

candidates.name: Falkirk Wheel
candidates.story: The rotating boat lift used segmented arms with high-strength friction-grip bolted site joints. The joint design accommodated transport and the fatigue from repeated rotation. The completed lift opened in 2002.
candidates.art_direction: Show the wheel under assembly beside the aqueduct, with a crane lifting an arm segment into position and a visible bolted flange joint. Use contractor and engineering records to establish the erection sequence and the opposed arms and gondola-ring geometry.

sources.name: BCSA/SCI New Steel Construction · SSDA 2002 Falkirk Wheel engineering account
